bullets.title: GOOGL Q2: Record Cloud growth but capex surge triggers AH selloff
bullets.body: Alphabet Q2 revenue +24% YoY to $119.8B beat consensus ($117B); Google Cloud +82% YoY to $24.77B crushed $22.46B est. and hit ~$100B run-rate. However, company raised FY26 capex guidance to $195-205B (from $180-190B) and FCF turned negative for the first time, sending stock -3-4.5% AH. CFO flagged modest margin pressure from third-party capacity and WIZ acquisition. Gemini at 950M MAU; 22B API tokens/min. Multiple banks cut PTs (Piper Sandler to $395, Oppenheimer to $400, JPM to $420).

bullets.title: TSLA Q2: Revenue beats but massive margin/EPS miss; FCF negative
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 revenue $28.24B beat $26.32B est (+26% YoY) but adj. EPS $0.33 missed $0.51-0.55 consensus badly; auto gross margin ex-reg credits 16.3% vs 18.4% expected; FCF -$1.09B (first negative in 2+ years) on $5.79B capex. Musk reaffirmed aggressive capex for AI/robotics/autonomy for next 2-3 years and called Optimus 'our biggest product ever.' Robotaxi live in 6 US cities; Model S/X lines decommissioned for Optimus production. Stock fell ~4% AH; Canaccord cut PT to $410.

bullets.title: TXN Q2: Broad semiconductor beat signals non-datacenter recovery
bullets.body: Texas Instruments Q2 revenue $5.46B beat $5.24B est, EPS $2.14 beat $1.93 est, FCF $2.74B crushed $1.82B est with capex well below forecast at $514M vs $676M. Q3 guidance $5.65-6.15B above consensus $5.62B. Analyst read-through: semiconductor recovery broadening beyond datacenter into wider industrial/analog demand.

bullets.title: NOW beats earnings; post-market among the winners
bullets.body: ServiceNow reported EPS $0.90 vs $0.86 estimate and revenue $3.98B vs $3.93B estimate, gaining ~4.73% after hours—standout outperformer vs. the TSLA/GOOGL misses in the same session.

bullets.title: AMD: CPU LTAs with Chinese AI DC customers; prices up 40%+ YTD
bullets.body: Intel and AMD are pursuing multi-year long-term server CPU supply agreements with major Chinese AI data center customers as prices surge 40%+ YTD and month-on-month increases top 10% for some products. Separately, AMD expanded its strategic partnership with Anthropic deploying Instinct MI455X GPUs; AMD also investing $5B equity in Anthropic alongside a 2GW MI450 deal.

bullets.title: GOOGL capex bullish for LITE: 'disproportionate beneficiary of TPU growth'
bullets.body: One fintwit account explicitly flagged LITE as disproportionately benefiting from Google's capex and TPU infrastructure spending. Separately, traders are bullish on CPO names AAOI and LITE following NVIDIA's volume manufacturing commentary on CPO switches for scale-out networking.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang says US has 'nothing to fear' from China's open-source AI
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang stated the US should not ban or restrict Chinese AI models and that 'there is no scenario where China runs US companies off the road.' Separately, Kimi K3 was noted as outperforming NVIDIA's own Nemotron 3 Ultra, with internal criticism that NVIDIA's committee-based training structure is hampering open-source competitiveness. NVDA also showed a $350M call wall at $215 drawing price higher.

bullets.title: META closes below 200-day MA; historical analog shows 21% drop risk
bullets.body: META just closed below its 200-day moving average; the last time the stock broke below that level it fell 21% over the next 9 weeks. One trader suggested buying META as a relative play off GOOGL weakness, while the stock's negative FCF status was also flagged by multiple accounts.

bullets.title: MU: YMTC surpasses Micron in NAND market share per third-party data
bullets.body: According to authoritative third-party data cited on X, YMTC has surpassed both Micron and SanDisk in NAND market share and is within 0.4 percentage points of Kioxia. Separately, Elon Musk noted Micron gave Tesla a 'significant allocation' of memory chips. Author clarified that an earlier warning about YMTC was not a sell signal and that NAND remains in short supply.

bullets.title: INTC: Ohio fab seeks operating partner; potential SK Hynix JV
bullets.body: Intel is seeking an operating partner for its delayed $28B Ohio chip campus with SK Hynix among candidates being evaluated. A separate tweet flagged a potential Intel-Hynix joint venture. Intel also announced a security partnership with Fortinet and will report earnings after market close Thursday.

bullets.title: TSEM: 300mm SiPh capacity expansion underway alongside UMC
bullets.body: TSEM is expanding to 300mm silicon photonics production capacity alongside UMC's mass production ramp. A separate post highlighted TSEM's process control credentials vs. competitors, citing a rival chip defect as validating TSEM's quality differentiation.

bullets.title: NOK Q2: Optical strong; IP Networks inflection is the key watch
bullets.body: Nokia reported Q2 with optical segment previously growing 20% while IP Networks grew only 3%; management had flagged IP improvement coming—that inflection is the key metric traders are watching. Nokia is also acquiring an NXP Arizona fab for InP optical production, with full conversion targeted by Q1 2029. AI & Cloud orders grew significantly in Q1.

bullets.title: GEV Q2: Electricity investment cycle now in contracted, multi-year commitments
bullets.body: GE Vernova's Q2 2026 call provided 'unusually strong' evidence that the global electricity investment cycle has progressed from forecast demand into contracted, prepaid, multi-year infrastructure commitments. TD Cowen raised PT to $1,235 from $1,220; RBC lifted to $1,225. One fintwit account flagged hedge funds getting 'rinsed' in GEV on the day.

bullets.title: DeepSeek/Wenfeng investor call leak: 10-month payback, Huawei GPU ramp, CUDA threat
bullets.body: Leaked DeepSeek investor call details: targeting 10-month payback on AI infrastructure using PDD playbook; securing ~16K Huawei AI chips; TileLang and AI-powered code generation seen reducing CUDA dependency barriers. Wenfeng also articulated a Nvidia bear case and estimated China's AI gap vs. US at 12-18 months.

bullets.title: AMD bullish: Coding AI to accelerate ROCm; Claude Code for chip design
bullets.body: One fintwit account argues advances in coding AI will naturally accelerate ROCm development, helping close the CUDA gap. AMD is also investing in Anthropic and will use Claude Code for chip design and software—a structural catalyst for the ROCm software ecosystem.

bullets.title: Macro: Japan yields hit multi-decade highs; yen at 40-year lows; oil surges
bullets.body: Japan's 2-year JGB yield hit 1.50%, highest since May 1995. Yen fell to its weakest vs. USD in 40 years. US 30-year Treasury yield traded above 5% on 27 days YTD, most since pre-GFC. Brent crude settled at $94/bbl (+3.4%) on Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers and US-Iran escalation; WTI above $86. Market now prices 31.5% odds of a July Fed rate hike vs. 10.7% a week ago.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning stretched; S&P guidance beats at record margin
bullets.body: Hedge fund momentum positioning and gross leverage near 5-year highs per one macro account. Separately, Mag-7 hedge fund positioning at 25th percentile suggesting underweight. S&P 500 corporate earnings guidance is beating analyst estimates by the largest margin on record.

bullets.title: Software sector down 15% YTD; PE hunting for 'SaaS-pocalypse' bargains
bullets.body: IGV software ETF is down 15% YTD. Private equity groups are now actively hunting SaaS bargains amid the sector's sustained weakness. The Nasdaq 100 has closed below its 50-day MA for 6 straight days, the longest stretch since April.

bullets.title: SMCI: Only tier-one OEM for unconventional server architectures
bullets.body: Supermicro positioned as the only tier-one OEM capable of supporting custom PCIe topologies and ARM-based compute solutions for AI startups, giving it a structural advantage as inference-optimized rack design diverges from training infrastructure.

bullets.title: AI capex sustainability debate: Anthropic/OpenAI on pace for $250B+ ARR
bullets.body: Multiple accounts pushed back on the 'AI capex is unsustainable' narrative, arguing Anthropic and OpenAI combined are on pace for $250B+ annual recurring revenue by year-end; $700B in 2026 AI capex amortized over 5 years implies viable unit economics. The counter-argument: Google has generated only ~$30B in excess cloud earnings on $140B in capex since Q1 2024.
